chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ya'qub ibn Yaqtin said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, when the Dhuhr prayer comes, we are unable to look at the time until they descend, so we descend with them and pray, then they rise and hurry, so we rise and pray Asr, and we show them as if we are bowing. Then they descend for Asr and put us forward, so we pray with them.' He said, 'Pray with them, may God bless them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying behind people who pray quickly or imperfectly?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *al-riwa' wa al-suhul* (ease and leniency) in congregational prayer, where the Imam or follower prioritizes the validity and unity of the prayer over strict adherence to individual precision. Imam al-Hasan (AS) advises praying behind those who may rush or lack perfect form, emphasizing that the communal act of worship outweighs minor imperfections, thereby fostering social cohesion and avoiding division among the believers.
